column1: # Strategy
Accountability|Responsibility for explaining decisions, completing agreed work, and addressing its results.|The project lead accepts accountability for checking the release before launch.
Action plan|A list of practical steps, owners, and timing for reaching a goal.|Our action plan assigns the sample, customer interview, and cost review to named people.
Acquisition|Buying control of another business, or gaining a customer, depending on context.|The owner compared acquiring a small supplier with building the capability internally.
Agile|An approach that develops work in small cycles and adapts through feedback.|The team used an agile approach to test one feature before planning the next.
Alignment|Agreement between goals, decisions, and the work people actually perform.|We checked alignment between the course objective and the practice task.
Annual report|A report covering an organization's activities and financial results for a year.|The board reviewed the annual report before discussing next year's priorities.
Assumption|Something treated as true for planning before it has been fully established.|Our estimate assumes ten orders a week; customer testing will check that assumption.
Audit trail|A record showing what changed, when, and by whom.|The audit trail helped us identify who approved the invoice adjustment.
Benchmark|A reference point used to compare performance, quality, or cost.|We compared delivery time with last quarter's benchmark.
Business continuity|Preparation for keeping important operations running through a disruption.|Our business continuity plan includes an alternate way to receive customer requests.
Business development|Work that builds opportunities, partnerships, or markets for a business.|The business development team met potential partners for a joint workshop.
Business ethics|Principles used to judge responsible conduct in business decisions.|Business ethics guided our decision to correct a misleading product claim.
Business case|An explanation of a proposed change, its benefits, costs, risks, and alternatives.|The business case compared a new booking system with improving the existing one.
Business intelligence|Organized information and analysis used to understand business performance.|Our business intelligence report showed which products generated repeat orders.
Capacity planning|Estimating the resources needed to handle expected work.|Capacity planning revealed that one reviewer could not handle the proposed launch volume.
Change management|A structured way to help people and processes adjust to a change.|Change management included training, feedback, and support for the new scheduling tool.
Code of conduct|Written expectations for how people should behave in an organization.|The code of conduct explains how staff should report conflicts of interest.
Competitor analysis|Studying other offers to understand customer choices and market differences.|Competitor analysis showed that buyers wanted clearer delivery estimates.
Core competency|A capability that is especially important to an organization's value.|Writing accessible lessons is a core competency of the learning studio.
Corporate governance|The systems through which an organization is directed and overseen.|Corporate governance sets responsibilities for management and the board.
Corporate social responsibility|A business's efforts to address its effects on people, communities, and the environment.|Our corporate social responsibility plan includes reducing packaging waste.
Cost-benefit analysis|Comparing a choice's expected benefits with its costs and tradeoffs.|A cost-benefit analysis showed that a simpler tool met our needs.
Critical success factor|A condition that is particularly important for reaching a goal.|Reliable order delivery is a critical success factor for the new shop.
Decision matrix|A table that compares options using chosen criteria.|Our decision matrix compared tools by accessibility, cost, and data handling.
Due diligence|Careful investigation before making a significant agreement or investment.|We checked records, risks, and obligations during due diligence on the supplier.
Economies of scale|Lower average cost that can result from producing or buying at greater volume.|A larger print run reduced the cost per copy, illustrating economies of scale.
Efficiency|How well a process uses resources to produce its result.|The new template improved efficiency by reducing repeated formatting work.
Effectiveness|How well an action achieves its intended result.|We assessed effectiveness by checking whether learners could perform the task.
Enterprise|An organized business or undertaking; the meaning depends on context.|The family enterprise sells products through several online channels.
Environmental scan|A review of outside conditions that may affect an organization.|An environmental scan considered customer habits, technology, and supplier changes.
Execution|Carrying out a plan through actual actions and decisions.|The strategy was clear, but execution required owners and weekly reviews.
Exit strategy|A plan for ending or transferring an owner's involvement in a business.|The founder's exit strategy considered a sale and a planned succession.
Feasibility study|An investigation of whether a proposed project can reasonably work.|The feasibility study examined demand, delivery capacity, and costs.
First-mover advantage|A possible benefit from entering a market before competing offers.|Early entry gave the company recognition, but first-mover advantage did not guarantee lasting demand.
Franchise|A business arrangement allowing an operator to use a brand and system under agreed terms.|The prospective owner reviewed the franchise agreement and operating obligations.
Go-to-market strategy|A plan for bringing an offer to a defined audience and generating demand.|Our go-to-market strategy starts with one customer group and one tested message.
Growth strategy|A plan for increasing a business's customers, revenue, or capabilities.|The growth strategy focuses on repeat customers before entering another market.
Innovation|Introducing a useful new approach, product, or process.|Innovation improved the booking experience rather than simply adding more features.
Joint venture|An arrangement in which parties work together on a business undertaking.|The firms formed a joint venture to develop a shared product.
Knowledge management|Organizing and sharing what an organization knows so people can use it.|Knowledge management keeps reviewed instructions accessible to new staff.
Market research|Collecting evidence about customers, demand, competitors, and market conditions.|Market research combined customer interviews with a review of existing offers.
Market share|A business's portion of sales or activity in a defined market.|We stated the region and product category when estimating market share.
Merger|Combining organizations under an agreed ownership or operating structure.|The merger required careful planning for staff, systems, and customer records.
Operating model|How a business organizes people, processes, and resources to deliver value.|The operating model defines who sells, fulfills, reviews, and supports each order.
Opportunity cost|The value of the best alternative given up when making a choice.|Time spent building an extra feature had the opportunity cost of delayed customer testing.
Outsourcing|Arranging for an outside provider to perform work.|We considered outsourcing printing while retaining design and quality review.
Partnership|A relationship in which people or organizations work together; legal meanings vary.|The studio and library agreed on responsibilities for their workshop partnership.
PESTLE analysis|A framework for examining political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental influences.|Our PESTLE analysis identified changes that could affect the delivery model.
Positioning|How an offer is presented as a fit for a particular audience and need.|Positioning the guide for first-time sellers made its purpose clearer.
Procurement|The process of obtaining goods or services for an organization.|Procurement included comparing suppliers, approving the purchase, and checking delivery.
Quality assurance|Planned activities intended to prevent problems and maintain quality.|Quality assurance included reviewed standards before lesson production began.
Quality control|Checking outputs to find whether they meet the required standards.|Quality control caught a damaged print before it reached a customer.
Resource allocation|Deciding how to distribute time, money, people, or equipment.|Resource allocation gave the highest-priority project enough review time.
Risk management|Identifying, evaluating, and responding to things that may affect objectives.|Risk management included a backup supplier and a recovery plan.
Scalability|A system's ability to handle more work without an unacceptable loss of performance or value.|We tested scalability by increasing requests while checking response quality.
Service-level agreement|An agreement defining expected service and relevant responsibilities or measures.|The service-level agreement states response targets and how issues are escalated.
Strategic planning|Choosing longer-term goals and the approach for reaching them.|Strategic planning connected the year's projects to the studio's priorities.
Succession planning|Preparing for key responsibilities to pass to another person.|Succession planning included documenting approvals and training a replacement.
Supply chain|The connected organizations and steps that produce and deliver an offer.|A supply chain delay affected the shop's delivery estimates.
SWOT analysis|A review of strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats.|The SWOT analysis separated internal capabilities from outside conditions.
Unit economics|The revenue and costs associated with a defined unit, such as one sale or customer.|We checked unit economics before increasing advertising spend.
Value chain|The activities through which an organization creates and delivers value.|Mapping the value chain showed where customer support improved the offer.
Vertical integration|Combining control of different stages of production or distribution within a business.|Producing components internally was one possible form of vertical integration.
# Finance
Accounting period|The span of time covered by a set of financial records or statements.|The accountant prepared figures for the quarterly accounting period.
Accrued expense|A cost incurred but not yet paid or fully recorded through an invoice.|The company recorded an accrued expense for work already completed.
Allowance for doubtful accounts|An estimate of receivables that may not be collected.|The allowance for doubtful accounts reflected the risk of unpaid customer balances.
Bad debt|Money owed that is considered uncollectible under the applicable accounting treatment.|The bookkeeper reviewed the evidence before recording the unpaid balance as bad debt.
Bank reconciliation|Comparing bank activity with the business's records and resolving differences.|The bank reconciliation found a payment recorded twice in our ledger.
Break-even point|The activity level at which relevant revenue equals relevant costs.|Our break-even estimate shows how many sales cover the launch costs.
Capital expenditure|Spending on an asset expected to serve the business beyond the current period.|The equipment purchase was evaluated as a capital expenditure.
Cash reserve|Money kept available to handle needs or unexpected expenses.|A cash reserve helped cover bills while customer payments were delayed.
Chart of accounts|The organized list of categories used to record financial transactions.|The chart of accounts separates sales, software, supplies, and equipment.
Contribution margin|Sales revenue minus the variable costs associated with those sales.|The contribution margin shows what remains to cover fixed costs and profit.
Current asset|An asset expected to be used or converted to cash within the relevant short-term period.|The balance sheet lists cash and qualifying receivables as current assets.
Current liability|An obligation expected to be settled within the relevant short-term period.|The unpaid supplier bill appears among current liabilities.
Depreciation|Allocating an eligible tangible asset's cost over its useful life for accounting or tax purposes.|The accountant reviewed depreciation for the studio's equipment.
Dividend|A distribution a company makes to shareholders, subject to its decisions and rules.|The shareholder received a dividend declared by the company.
Double-entry bookkeeping|Recording transactions with balancing entries in at least two accounts.|Double-entry bookkeeping records both the cash received and the related sale.
EBITDA|Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization; a measure with limitations.|The analyst compared EBITDA but also checked actual cash needs.
Financial statement|A structured report describing a business's financial position or performance.|The lender asked for current financial statements rather than unsupported estimates.
Fiscal year|The annual period an organization uses for financial reporting.|Our fiscal year ends on June 30 rather than December 31.
Fixed cost|A cost that does not change directly with activity within a relevant range.|Monthly rent is a fixed cost within our current operating plan.
General ledger|The main accounting record that organizes transactions by account.|The bookkeeper traced the equipment entry through the general ledger.

Goodwill|In acquisition accounting, an amount reflecting purchase value beyond identified net assets under the applicable rules.|The acquisition's goodwill required review under the relevant accounting standards.
Gross margin|Gross profit expressed as a percentage of revenue.|We calculated gross margin using the same revenue and cost definitions each month.
Inventory|Goods or materials held for sale or use in production.|The inventory count identified items that had not yet been sold.
Liquidity|The ability to meet cash needs or convert assets to cash without undue difficulty.|The company reviewed liquidity before committing to a large purchase.
Markup|An amount added to cost when setting a selling price.|A markup on cost is not the same percentage as margin on sales.
Net income|Revenue remaining after the expenses included in an income calculation.|The statement shows net income after the listed business expenses.
Operating expense|A cost associated with running a business's normal activities.|Hosting and routine office supplies are operating expenses in our records.
Operating profit|Profit from operations before certain nonoperating items, depending on the reporting framework.|We reviewed operating profit separately from the gain on selling equipment.
Overhead|Costs that support operations but are not directly assigned to a specific unit in the same way as direct costs.|Rent and administrative software contribute to overhead.
Profit and loss statement|Another name for an income statement showing revenue, expenses, and resulting profit or loss.|The owner used the profit and loss statement to review the quarter.
Purchase order|A buyer's document specifying an order and its terms.|The supplier checked quantities against the purchase order.
Retained earnings|Accumulated earnings kept in a company after distributions and relevant adjustments.|The balance sheet reports retained earnings as part of equity.
Return on investment|A comparison of a return with the investment required, using a stated calculation.|We explained the costs and time period included in the return on investment estimate.
Solvency|The ability to meet financial obligations over time.|The adviser reviewed solvency using obligations and the company's resources.
Trial balance|A list of ledger balances used to check that total debits and credits agree.|A balanced trial balance does not prove every transaction was classified correctly.
Variable cost|A cost that changes with activity such as production or sales.|Packaging is a variable cost because more orders use more packages.
Variance|The difference between an actual result and a planned or comparison amount.|The spending variance led us to investigate higher shipping costs.
Write-off|An accounting reduction or removal of a recorded amount; its meaning depends on context.|The accountant reviewed the evidence and rules before approving a write-off.
Yield|A return measure expressed relative to an investment's value using a specified method.|We checked which yield calculation the report used before comparing investments.
Zero-based budgeting|Building a budget by justifying planned spending rather than simply carrying forward last period's amounts.|Zero-based budgeting required each team to explain its proposed costs.
# Funding
Angel investor|An individual who invests in a business, often at an early stage, under agreed terms.|The founder discussed ownership and expectations with an angel investor.
Balloon payment|A large payment due at the end of certain financing arrangements.|The owner checked whether cash would be available for the balloon payment.
Business credit|A business's credit relationships and payment history as assessed by providers.|The supplier reviewed business credit before offering payment terms.
Credit limit|The maximum borrowing or spending amount permitted under a credit arrangement.|The business stayed within its approved credit limit.
Credit score|A model-based measure used to summarize aspects of credit risk.|The provider explained which credit score it considered and what else it reviewed.
Debt-to-equity ratio|A comparison of debt with equity using stated balance-sheet amounts.|We specified which liabilities were included in the debt-to-equity ratio.
Default|Failure to meet an obligation under the terms of an agreement.|The contract explains what constitutes default and the available remedies.
Disbursement|The release or payment of funds.|The business scheduled the equipment purchase after confirming the disbursement date.
Factoring|Selling or assigning eligible receivables to a factor under agreed terms.|The owner compared factoring costs with waiting for customer payment.
Financial covenant|A contractual condition requiring particular financial measures or conduct.|The loan's financial covenant requires regular reporting and a stated ratio.
Grace period|A stated period during which certain consequences or charges may not apply, depending on the agreement.|We read the contract rather than assuming a grace period existed.
Installment|One of a series of payments under a payment schedule.|The monthly installment includes the amounts specified in the agreement.
Loan term|The period and related conditions of a loan arrangement.|The business compared the loan term with the equipment's useful life.
Personal guarantee|An individual's promise to be responsible for specified business obligations under agreed terms.|The owner sought advice before signing the personal guarantee.
Prepayment penalty|A charge that may apply when an obligation is paid early under certain terms.|The borrower checked whether the contract included a prepayment penalty.
Repayment schedule|The timing and amounts of payments required under a financing agreement.|The cash plan accounts for the repayment schedule and slower customer payments.
Secured loan|A loan supported by specified collateral under its terms.|The secured loan agreement identifies the pledged equipment.
Term loan|A loan with a defined repayment period and agreed payment terms.|The owner compared a term loan with a credit line for the purchase.
Unsecured loan|A loan not supported by specified collateral, though other obligations may still apply.|The provider explained that unsecured did not mean obligation-free.
Venture capital|Investment in businesses with growth potential through specialized investors or funds.|The founder evaluated venture capital alongside its ownership and growth expectations.
# Marketing
Attribution|Assigning credit to interactions that contributed to a result under a chosen model.|Our attribution report does not prove that one ad caused every sale.
Audience segment|A subgroup of an audience sharing relevant characteristics or needs.|We created an audience segment for first-time course creators.
Bounce rate|An analytics measure of visits that meet the platform's defined bounce criteria.|The analyst checked the platform's bounce rate definition before comparing reports.
Brand awareness|How familiar people are with a brand.|The campaign measures brand awareness separately from purchases.
Brand identity|The visual, verbal, and other elements used to express a brand.|Our brand identity uses a consistent name, logo, and tone.
Brand voice|The recognizable way a brand communicates through words.|The editor revised the draft to match our clear, human brand voice.
Buyer persona|A research-informed description of a representative customer type.|The buyer persona was revised after real customer interviews.
Campaign|A coordinated set of activities directed toward a marketing goal.|The campaign connects a helpful video, a page, and an inquiry form.
Channel|A route used to communicate with or reach an audience.|Email is one channel in our customer follow-up plan.
Churn|The loss of customers, subscribers, or revenue over a defined period.|We stated the period and customer group when measuring churn.
Content calendar|A schedule organizing what content will be published and when.|The content calendar leaves time for review before release.
Copywriting|Writing intended to explain an offer and encourage a relevant action.|Copywriting made the service's scope and next step clear.
Cost per click|Advertising cost divided by the counted clicks.|We calculated cost per click using the campaign's reported spend.
Cost per lead|Marketing cost divided by the counted leads under a stated definition.|The team checked lead quality alongside cost per lead.
Customer journey|The path a person takes through discovering, evaluating, using, and receiving support for an offer.|Mapping the customer journey revealed missing delivery information.
Customer retention|Keeping customers engaged or purchasing over time.|Clear support and reliable delivery helped customer retention.
Direct marketing|Communicating an offer directly to a selected audience.|The team reviewed permission and applicable rules before direct marketing by email.
Email marketing|Using email to share relevant information and offers with an audience.|Email marketing directed subscribers to the new lesson.
Evergreen content|Content designed to stay useful beyond a short news cycle.|The definition guide is evergreen content, though examples still need review.
Influencer marketing|Promotion involving people whose audience may be relevant to an offer.|The influencer marketing agreement requires accurate claims and appropriate disclosures.
Landing page|A page designed around a particular visitor goal or campaign.|The landing page answers the buyer's main questions before offering a next step.
Lead magnet|A useful resource offered to encourage an audience action, often signup.|The checklist is a lead magnet with a clear explanation of the signup process.
Lead nurturing|Providing relevant information to help potential customers evaluate an offer over time.|Lead nurturing answered common questions without pressuring the buyer.
Market segmentation|Dividing a market into groups for more relevant research or offers.|Market segmentation separated household buyers from institutional purchasers.
Marketing mix|The coordinated choices used to bring an offer to market.|We reviewed product, price, place, and promotion as part of the marketing mix.
Media kit|A package describing a brand, audience, or publication for potential collaborators.|The media kit includes verified audience information and contact details.
Newsletter|A recurring publication sent or made available to an audience.|The newsletter summarizes new learning resources each month.
Pay-per-click|An advertising model in which charges are tied to qualifying clicks.|The pay-per-click test has a budget and a clear measure of useful inquiries.
Referral marketing|Encouraging or enabling existing contacts to recommend an offer.|Referral marketing worked best when the customer could explain the value clearly.
Remarketing|Reaching people again after relevant previous interactions, subject to the tools and permissions used.|The team reviewed privacy settings before starting remarketing.
Return on ad spend|Revenue attributed to advertising divided by the advertising spend under a specified method.|Return on ad spend is not the same as profit after all costs.
Social proof|Evidence from other people's experience that may influence a decision.|Verified customer examples provided social proof without invented reviews.
Split testing|Comparing variants to learn how a change affects a result.|Split testing compared two calls to action while other conditions stayed similar.
Unique selling proposition|A clear reason an offer stands apart for its intended customer.|The unique selling proposition focuses on a practical benefit we can support.
User-generated content|Material created by users rather than the brand itself.|The shop requested permission before reusing user-generated content.
Viral content|Content that spreads rapidly through sharing; virality is not a guaranteed business outcome.|The viral content brought attention, but we still checked the relevance of new visitors.
Word of mouth|Information or recommendations passed between people.|Word of mouth grew after customers had a reliable experience.
# Sales
Account management|Maintaining customer relationships and coordinating their ongoing needs.|Account management includes checking delivery and answering renewal questions.
Average order value|Revenue divided by the counted orders for a specified period.|We reviewed average order value alongside margin and repeat purchasing.
B2B|Business-to-business activity in which the customer is another business.|The B2B workshop helps organizations train their employees.
B2C|Business-to-consumer activity in which the customer is an individual consumer.|The shop's B2C offer is designed for home use.
Cart abandonment|Starting a purchase process without completing it, under the platform's measurement definition.|Unexpected shipping charges contributed to cart abandonment.
Checkout|The stage where a buyer reviews and completes a purchase.|The checkout clearly displays the price before payment.
Close|Complete an agreement or sale; the exact event should be defined.|The team counts a close only after the customer accepts the agreement.
Cross-selling|Offering a complementary product or service.|The shop uses cross-selling to suggest a compatible template.
Customer service|Helping customers understand, use, or resolve problems with an offer.|Customer service verified the order before discussing the available options.
Discount|A reduction from a stated price under defined conditions.|The discount applies only to the products listed in the offer.
E-commerce|Buying and selling through electronic channels.|Our e-commerce page explains delivery and support before purchase.
Fulfillment|Preparing and delivering what a customer ordered.|Fulfillment includes packaging, dispatch, and the delivery information.
Lead qualification|Checking whether a potential customer fits relevant criteria for an offer.|Lead qualification asks about needs and scope rather than assuming every inquiry fits.
Negotiation|Working toward an agreement through discussion of interests and terms.|Negotiation clarified the project scope and revision limits.
Objection|A concern or reason a potential customer raises about an offer.|The buyer's objection revealed uncertainty about compatibility.
Pipeline|The set of opportunities moving through a defined process.|The sales pipeline separates new inquiries from confirmed orders.
Price elasticity|How strongly demand responds to a change in price under specified conditions.|The analyst treated price elasticity as an estimate rather than a universal rule.
Pricing strategy|An approach to setting prices in relation to costs, value, and the market.|Our pricing strategy includes delivery work and ongoing support.
Proposal|A document or presentation describing a proposed offer or project.|The proposal states scope, price, assumptions, and responsibilities.
Prospect|A person or organization that may become a customer.|The prospect asked for evidence that the service fits their needs.
Quote|A stated price and relevant conditions for a specified offer.|The customer reviewed the quote's scope and validity period.
Refund|Returning money under the applicable circumstances and terms.|Support checked the purchase and policy before arranging a refund.
Renewal|Continuing an agreement or subscription for another period.|The renewal notice explains timing and current terms.
Sales cycle|The steps and time from an initial sales opportunity to an outcome.|The team reviewed which part of the sales cycle created delays.
Service recovery|Actions taken to address a service failure and restore a useful experience.|Service recovery included a clear explanation and the agreed correction.
Subscription|Access or delivery provided on a recurring basis under agreed terms.|The subscription page explains billing and cancellation.
Upselling|Offering a higher-level or more extensive option.|Upselling is useful only when the larger option fits the customer's need.
Wholesale|Selling goods, often in quantity, to businesses rather than final consumers.|The wholesaler supplies products to independent shops.
# Operations
Acceptance criteria|Conditions used to decide whether a result meets the agreed need.|The acceptance criteria require a working form and a tested mobile layout.
Backlog|A prioritized collection of work waiting to be done.|The backlog separates urgent corrections from optional features.
Batch processing|Handling a group of items together rather than individually as they arrive.|Batch processing prepares the day's invoices for review.
Change request|A recorded proposal to alter agreed work or requirements.|The change request explains how payment processing affects the launch plan.
Cycle time|The time required to move an item through a defined portion of a process.|We measured cycle time from draft assignment to approval.
Deadline|The agreed time by which work is due.|The deadline includes enough time for the final review.
Escalation|Moving an issue to a person or level with suitable authority or expertise.|Escalation is required when support cannot authorize the requested action.
Exception handling|A defined response to cases that do not follow the ordinary process.|Exception handling explains what happens when an order record is missing.
Handoff|Transferring work or responsibility from one person or step to another.|The handoff includes the draft, source notes, and open questions.
Kanban|A visual approach for managing work through stages and limiting work in progress.|Our Kanban board shows items waiting, active, and ready for review.
Lead time|The time between a defined request and its fulfillment.|We state the start and finish points when reporting lead time.
Process map|A diagram or list showing how work moves through steps.|The process map identifies the input, review point, and final output.
Quality standard|A stated requirement for the characteristics or performance of work.|The quality standard requires readable labels and verified facts.
Rework|Work repeated or corrected because the earlier result was incomplete or unsuitable.|Clearer briefs reduced rework during lesson production.
Root cause|An underlying factor contributing to a problem, rather than only its visible symptom.|The root cause of missed replies was unclear ownership.
Sprint|A bounded work period used in certain iterative development approaches.|The sprint focuses on a small tested feature rather than the entire site.
Throughput|The amount of work completed over a defined time.|Throughput rose after the team resolved the review bottleneck.
Work in progress|Work that has started but is not yet finished.|Limiting work in progress helped the team complete its highest-priority tasks.
# People
Active listening|Listening to understand, checking meaning, and responding to what was actually said.|Active listening helped the leader identify the concern behind a complaint.
Coaching|Helping someone develop through questions, practice, observation, and feedback.|Coaching gave the new reviewer a chance to explain their decision.
Conflict of interest|A situation where personal interests may improperly influence a responsibility.|The evaluator disclosed a conflict of interest before the supplier review.
Delegation|Assigning responsibility and suitable authority for work while keeping expectations clear.|Delegation included a spending limit and a check-in date.
Employee onboarding|Helping a new employee understand and begin their role.|Employee onboarding includes tools, responsibilities, and a supported first task.
Empowerment|Giving people meaningful ability and support to make relevant decisions.|Empowerment includes clear boundaries rather than simply more responsibility.
Human resources|The function supporting employment-related systems, people, and processes.|Human resources coordinates hiring records and staff policies.
Job description|A statement of a role's work, responsibilities, and relevant requirements.|The job description names tasks rather than only a broad title.
Leadership|Helping people move toward a useful shared result through influence and responsibility.|Leadership made the purpose clear and invited concerns about the plan.
Mentoring|A developmental relationship in which a more experienced person shares guidance.|Mentoring helped the learner compare career options and next steps.
Performance review|A structured discussion of work, evidence, expectations, and development.|The performance review used specific examples and agreed actions.
Psychological safety|A shared sense that people can raise relevant questions or concerns without inappropriate punishment.|Psychological safety helped the team report a mistake early.
Recruitment|Finding and assessing people for roles.|Recruitment uses the actual tasks and requirements of the position.
Remote work|Work performed away from a central workplace using suitable communication and systems.|Remote work requires clear access, responsibilities, and communication practices.
Retention|Keeping employees, customers, or other participants over time, depending on context.|The report specifies employee retention rather than customer retention.
Servant leadership|A leadership approach emphasizing service to people's development and shared work.|Servant leadership led the manager to remove barriers for the team.
Situational leadership|Adapting leadership behavior to the needs of the task and people.|Situational leadership used coaching for a new task and delegation for a familiar one.
Team charter|An agreement describing a team's purpose, roles, and ways of working.|The team charter explains how decisions and disagreements are handled.
Transformational leadership|A leadership approach that builds shared purpose and encourages meaningful change.|Transformational leadership connected the new process to the organization's mission.
# Technology
Algorithm|A defined set of steps for carrying out a computation or solving a problem.|The sorting algorithm orders requests by a stated rule.
Authentication|Checking that a person or system is who it claims to be.|Authentication verifies the account before access is granted.
Authorization|Deciding what an identified person or system is permitted to do.|Authorization allows the reviewer to read a record but not alter billing.
Backup|A separate copy kept to help restore information if the original is lost or damaged.|We tested the backup by restoring a sample file.
Cloud computing|Accessing computing resources through services rather than only local equipment.|Cloud computing provides storage and processing through an external service.
Data breach|Unauthorized access to or exposure of protected information.|The response plan explains how to handle a suspected data breach.
Database|An organized collection of data managed for retrieval and use.|The database connects each order with its approved customer record.
Domain name|A human-readable internet name used to locate a service.|The domain name points visitors to the studio's website.
Encryption|Transforming information so it cannot be read without the relevant means of decoding it.|Encryption helps protect records, but access controls still matter.
Firewall|A system that filters network traffic according to rules.|The firewall restricts traffic that the organization does not allow.
Hosting|Making website or application resources available through a server or service.|The hosting provider serves the site's files to visitors.
Identity verification|Checking evidence related to a claimed identity.|Identity verification uses approved procedures rather than a familiar profile picture alone.
Least privilege|Giving an account or tool only the access needed for its task.|Least privilege lets the assistant read the approved folder without accessing every record.
Metadata|Information describing other data, such as its author, format, or creation date.|The editor checks the document's metadata before publication.
Multifactor authentication|Using more than one distinct type of evidence to verify access.|Multifactor authentication adds a check beyond the password.
Open source|Software made available under a license that permits specified access, use, modification, and sharing.|We reviewed the open-source license before reusing the code.
Phishing|A deceptive attempt to obtain information or actions by posing as a trusted source.|The suspected phishing message asked for a login code through an unfamiliar link.
Software as a service|Software accessed as an ongoing service, often through a browser.|The team reviewed the software-as-a-service terms and data practices.
Version control|Tracking changes to files so versions can be reviewed and coordinated.|Version control lets us compare the change with the previous working build.
Webhook|A message sent automatically to a specified destination when an event occurs.|The webhook notifies the order system when a payment event is received.
# AI
AI agent|A system designed to take steps and use tools toward a goal within defined limits.|The AI agent drafts a reply but requires approval before sending.
Algorithmic bias|A pattern of systematic skew in a system's behavior or results.|The team tests for algorithmic bias across relevant user groups.
Context window|The amount of input and related material a model can consider in a given operation.|A document exceeding the context window may need a different review approach.
Embedding|A numerical representation used to compare or process features of data.|An embedding helps the search system find related passages.
Evaluation|Checking a system or result against stated criteria and representative cases.|Evaluation includes normal requests and cases with missing information.
Fine-tuning|Further training a model using a selected dataset for a particular purpose.|Fine-tuning changes training, unlike simply writing a longer prompt.
Inference|Using a trained model to produce a result from an input.|The app performs inference when it generates a reply.
Multimodal AI|AI that can process or produce more than one form of data, such as text and images.|Multimodal AI can interpret a picture together with its written question.
Natural language processing|Computational methods for working with human language.|Natural language processing helps categorize written customer requests.
Neural network|A computational model made of connected processing units with learned parameters.|The neural network learns patterns during training rather than understanding through human experience.

Prompt injection|An attempt to make a system follow unwanted instructions introduced through input or retrieved material.|The test document contains prompt injection that tries to bypass the review rule.
Retrieval-augmented generation|Combining retrieved information with generation to support a response.|Retrieval-augmented generation provides relevant records, but the answer still needs checking.
Supervised learning|Training with examples that include the target outputs or labels.|Supervised learning uses reviewed examples of correctly categorized requests.
Token|A unit into which a model divides data for processing; it need not equal a whole word.|The token count affects how much text fits into the model's input.
Training data|Examples used to adjust a model during training.|The team checks whether it has permission to use the training data.
Unsupervised learning|Learning patterns from data without supplied target labels for each example.|Unsupervised learning may identify groups of similar records.
# Design
Alt text|Text that communicates the relevant meaning of an image when it cannot be seen.|The chart's alt text describes its main finding rather than its colors alone.
CSS|Cascading Style Sheets, a language for defining the presentation of web content.|CSS sets the page's spacing, colors, and responsive layout.
Design system|Reusable patterns and guidance that keep interfaces consistent.|The design system specifies button behavior and readable form labels.

Circle back|Return to a topic later; a clear follow-up time makes it useful.|We will circle back on Friday with the verified costs.
Deep dive|A detailed investigation of a subject.|The deep dive examines the actual customer journey and its evidence.
Elevator pitch|A brief explanation of an idea or offer.|The elevator pitch names the customer, problem, and useful result.
Quick win|An improvement that can be achieved relatively soon with limited effort.|Fixing the broken contact link is a quick win with a visible benefit.
Touch base|Make a brief contact or update.|The project owner will touch base after testing the sample.
Win-win|An outcome intended to provide useful benefits to more than one party.|The team checked whether the proposed win-win actually met both partners' needs.
